summary: In all five passages the person surrounded speaks in the first person. Water, waves, cords and troubles supply the subjects of the verb.

senses.definition: Jonah describes waters closing around him, with seaweed bound around his head. David’s song uses waves of death in Samuel and cords of death in the Psalter. In each case the danger presses on him from every side.
Troubles beyond counting surround the speaker. Another psalm recalls the cords of death closing in before the speaker called upon Yahweh.

note: A proposed Akkadian comparison could not be confirmed in the available Akkadian glossary. The parallel songs and Jonah’s description establish the sense within Hebrew.
